decisions.issues: Clean. Nagoji matches the ch19 Ananthan Pillai row: topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, plain white mundu and shoulder cloth, heavy silver chain of office with a medallion, ivory-handled knife at the waist. He sits on the stone platform under the jackfruit tree, with kalari sparring beyond the wall and dark monsoon cloud building. Minor: the pale scar lines are on the top of the left forearm, not clearly the inner side, but they read as pale ridges with no emblem or letters. Both captions fit in the clear cloudy sky at upper right (x 0.55 to 0.85, y 0.02 to 0.25) or over the roof tiles at upper left.

Minor only. Padmini places the bundle into Nagoji's raised hand instead of tossing it into his lap, but the hand-over still reads. The sky is bright with white cloud, not a heavy bank building in the north. Nagoji has faint jaw shading and a small shadow under the lower lip. At reading size the chin reads clean-shaven. The grey at his temple is a broad streak. Padmini's grey threading is moderate, which the ch16-27 bible row allows. Everything else matches: flush gold ear stud, topknot, plain white mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain, ivory conch-marked knife, sound hands, and clear sky at the upper centre for Padmini's balloon.

Acceptable. The beat reads: the thin, sun-blackened boy squats on the kitchen steps with a black wool blanket over one shoulder and cracked bare feet, eating rice from a leaf by hand, with the kitchen hearth behind him. Padmini looks back over her shoulder, walking stick in hand, in the same jackfruit courtyard, with the kalari and the wet paving matching 1.1 and 1.2. Minor deviations: she looks back toward the reader (that is, toward Nagoji off-panel) rather than at the boy. The grey in her hair is much fainter than in 1.2, and her face is harder and a little younger than in 1.2, though close to her sheet. Both balloons fit in the open grey sky above and to the right of her head (x 0.2 to 0.65, y 0.0 to 0.17).

The rim of the silver chain medallion carries a ring of tiny coin-legend-like marks. At reading size they look like a notched border, and the upper-left caption should sit over the upper chest to cover the medallion (about x 0.24-0.35, y 0.13-0.20). The courtyard paving behind him is rain-wet with puddles while panel 1.2 shows dry ground. The chain is heavier and chunkier than the finer chain in 1.2. Otherwise the beat is right: close on the hands opening the cloth, grey-black dust sifting onto the white mundu, ridged discoloured nails, the pale ridged brand and long white scar on the left forearm, the ivory conch knife at the waist, and sound hands. Clear space for both captions: the upper chest band and the lower-left white mundu.

Acceptable. A folded sheet of paper, not palm leaf, opens in both hands, with sound anatomy. The over-the-shoulder view keeps the same jackfruit courtyard, kalari, wet paving and monsoon sky. Nagoji's profile shows the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, the gold stud and the shoulder cloth. Minor issues: (1) the ink marks are dense pseudo-cursive in a Latin-looking hand, illegible as the script requires but closer to a European letter than to Marathi Modi script; (2) the top of the head is cropped, so the topknot is not visible, and the hair at his visible temple shows no grey; (3) it is an over-the-shoulder view rather than a tight insert. Captions fit in the cloudy sky at upper right (x 0.62 to 0.85, y 0.0 to 0.2) or over the plain shoulder cloth at lower left (x 0.0 to 0.4, y 0.55 to 0.95), clear of his face and hands.

Minor: there are three small riders with a saffron swallow-tailed pennant in the left middle ground that the script does not call for. The flag is correct for the Deccan, but the riders anticipate 2.3. Otherwise the panel matches 2.1: dawn sun, cracked black-soil field, flat-roofed stone village, flat-topped hills, two tiny figures at the far edge of the field, a warm dry palette, a torn-paper edge and no text. The large pale sky (upper centre and right) is clear space for the letter caption.

Minor prop changes: the father carries a rope-lashed wooden pick rather than a plough (a plough appears behind the oxen in the background). His kambal hangs over both shoulders instead of one, and he is only slightly bent. It is hard to tell whether the mother's sari is tied kashta-style. The beat holds: the white-haired father in a white pheta, black kambal and dhoti shades his eyes at a cloudless white sky. The mother, with green glass bangles, turmeric hands and a seed basket on her hip, raises one hand mid-argument. Hands are sound and there is no text. The torn-paper edge and warm palette match. The wide white sky across the top right is clear space for both captions.

Minor: the two bands are closing head-on rather than shown mid-pass, and the blue sky is a little cooler than the warm dry letter palette. Otherwise the panel matches 2.3. A walled hill fort stands on a cliffed scarp, and two bands of riders in white angarkhas and pagdis face each other on the dusty road. One band rides under a saffron swallow-tailed pennant and the other under a plain dark red pennant, with no emblems or lettering. The riders eye each other with hands near their hilts. Horse and rider anatomy holds up, and the torn-paper edge is there. Open sky at top left and top right gives room for the two captions.

Minor only: the silver chain of office is not visible on the exposed chest (the 3.1 lock does not require it, but the chapter row does); a light stubble shadow on the chin still reads as clean-shaven; a fair amount of loose hair hangs below the topknot. Wet eyes, gold ear stud, thick curled moustache, smeared unreadable ink on the paper, and the jackfruit courtyard with kalari boys all match the script and page 1. Caption space: the cloudy sky at top right (x 0.6 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.25).

Clean. One figure: present-day Nagoji seen from behind at the right edge, with a high Kerala topknot, grey at the temples (a little more than 'first grey' but acceptable), a white shoulder cloth on a bare shoulder and a flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging. The Chapter 3 storm bleeds in as a ragged-edged stain, showing the heeled hull, boiling black water, a taut rope across the deck and the flooded square hatch. The courtyard survives at the edges: jackfruit tree, red-tile roofs and stone steps. There is no text and no painted boxes. The dark, low-detail storm sky in the upper-left quarter is the space for both captions. No face is visible (back of head only), so faces is empty. The courtyard floor is drawn wet while panel 3.1 is drier, which is a minor point.

Minor: the hairline graze is drawn with a reddish tint. It reads as a scrape, not running blood, but it is close to the no-blood rule. The wave rises around him rather than clearly over his head. Keshavrao matches his sheet (hacked short hair, faint moustache, torn grey-brown tunic, no ear stud) and wears iron manacles on both wrists. His eyes are wide and his mouth open, and the frayed, snapped rope end floats slack beside him. Hands and anatomy are sound. The panel has no lettering.

Minor only. The thumb presses flat on a folded sheaf held in the fist on his white-mundu lap, not on paper laid flat, but the script beat reads clearly: the ridged nail catches the light and the setting matches the courtyard (dappled shade on the stone platform, white mundu, consistent with 3.1 and 4.1). The knuckle is only slightly pale. The ink marks on the paper are soft, blurred smears with no legible glyphs, which fits the 'smeared, seen through tears' treatment in 3.1. The forearm shown is the outer side, so the inner-left scar is correctly out of view. Both captions can go in the top band of dappled stone platform and the upper right above the paper, clear of the thumb and nail. v01 (full face, a second man, kalari background, wide framing) and v02 (legible pseudo-script on the paper) are not listed as candidates and were not considered.

Minor: two sardars wear red pagdis, and the cross-legged one with folded arms also has a red waist cloth. The red-turban rule strictly covers background Maratha riders, but the foreground-right red-turbaned man with a gold ear stud should not be read as Nagoji. Caption space is only moderately clean: the best spot is the top band over the arch tops and the pale sky in the arch openings (x 0.25 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.18), which holds no faces or key action. Everything else matches the script: a warm letter palette with a torn-paper edge, a Pune darbar, sardars in pagdis and angarkhas, and an unlettered painted cloth map with blue river bands, fort pictograms and no subcontinent outline. The beat is clear: one leans back with folded arms, one spreads his hands, and one finger presses into the sea band at the bottom edge. Saffron swallow-tailed pennants. Hands are sound.

Clean. The beat is right: an afternoon courtyard with dappled shade, Nagoji tucking a blank folded letter into his mundu waist, Padmini a few steps off leaning on her stick, women carrying brass pots and boys in the kalari behind. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch19 row: greying topknot, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, silver chain, plain mundu and shoulder cloth, the ivory knife with the conch mark, and the long pale scar on his left forearm. There is no text in the art, and the hands are sound. Lettering space: the open sky between the tree and the right-hand roof takes Padmini's and Nagoji's balloons, and the canopy at top left takes the caption.

Minor only. Padmini's hair carries somewhat more grey streaking on top than the bible's 'light grey threading', though it is still mostly black and coiled at the nape, and it matches 4.1 and 4.3 closely enough. A small white highlight sits above Nagoji's right brow; it reads as light, not as a forehead mark. His topknot sits at the back of the crown with loose curls hanging, as on the later-life sheet. Everything else checks out. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a flush gold ear stud, a plain white mundu with no border, the shoulder cloth, the silver chain, the ivory-handled knife and the pale scar on his inner left forearm. Padmini stands with her stick planted and looks down at him. The setting matches the neighbouring panels: the same courtyard, jackfruit tree, stone platform and kalari pit, in afternoon light. Hands are sound, and there is no painted text or anachronism. Open sky between the two heads (about x 0.35 to 0.75, y 0.05 to 0.30) leaves room for the four short balloons.

Acceptable, with minor notes. Padmini is alone, in the same bright courtyard as 4.1 and 4.2. Her face, stick, cream-and-gold sari and gold jewellery match the sheet. She is walking with a stern sideways look rather than clearly nodding, but the nod is hard to show in a still and the expression carries the line. Three small points. First, no grey shows in her hair here, though the ch16-27 row asks for grey threads and 4.1 and 4.2 show them. Second, the stone platform under the jackfruit tree at right is empty, so a close reader may wonder where Nagoji went; he can be read as seated off-frame past the trunk. Third, the kalari boys in the background are tiny and fine. There is no text in the art. Lettering space: open sky at top centre for the balloon and low-detail paving at lower right or the canopy at top right for the caption.

Acceptable, with one art note. The beat is right: dusk in the same courtyard with the sky going blue, and Nagoji rising from the stone platform under the jackfruit tree, one hand pushing off the stone, looking toward the gate. A wiry, bare-chested runner comes through the courtyard entrance in a short hitched mundu, hair in a small knot, staff in hand, dust kicked up at his feet. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch19 row: greying topknot, moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, silver chain, shoulder cloth and the ivory knife. The lamps are brass with open flames, consistent with the period. There is no text, and the hands are sound. The note: the brand on his left forearm, near the elbow, is a dark curled hook-with-dot mark that reads more like a tattoo than the pale puckered patch on the inner forearm. It is small at print size and not letter-like or a cross, but it should be softened to a pale ridged patch in a retouch, and it will not match the regenerated 4.2. Lettering space: the large open dusk sky at top centre and right takes the caption and the runner's balloon.

Clean enough to use. Varma matches his sheet in full court dress (peacock-crest turban, pearl earrings, red forehead mark, pearl and gold necklaces, armlets, gold-bordered cream cloth) and holds a blank single sheet. Nagoji sits on the mat at right and matches: curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, topknot, plain white mundu with no border, shoulder cloth, silver chain, ivory-hilted knife, scar and brand on the inner left forearm with no letters. No guards, no text (the floor map is lines only). Minor: Nagoji's grey streak at the temple is a little heavier than 'first grey'. For lettering, Varma's balloon fits over the shelves at upper centre (x 0.35-0.62, y 0.02-0.2) and Nagoji's over the dark corridor ceiling at upper right (x 0.66-0.98, y 0.02-0.22), so both read in order.

Acceptable. Varma alone in the same room (brass lamp, red bolster, shelves of palm-leaf bundles and plain-spined volumes, doorway to the pillared corridor at right). He wears the sheet's court look and has a faint smile, looking right toward Nagoji, who is off panel. Hands are clasped and sound, and there is no text. Minor: no letter is visible in his hands or beside him, between 5.1 and 5.3. Plenty of plain laterite wall at upper centre (x 0.45-0.75, y 0.08-0.3) for the balloon.

Minor: at the very top-left edge, the underside of Varma's chin shows a small dark beard (about 0.06 x 0.05 of the frame). His sheet has a clean-shaven chin. No readable face is shown, and the first Varma balloon placed top-left, with its tail running up to the off-panel speaker, would cover it. Otherwise it is a clean insert. The ringed forefinger taps a line near the foot of the letter, and the letter carries only abstract ink dashes with nothing readable. The gold armlet, bangle and necklaces fit the court look. The room matches: laterite wall, palm-leaf shelves, rolled maps, cloth-bound volumes, brass oil lamp with an open wick and the pillared doorway. Hands are sound. Lettering space: upper laterite wall at centre and top-left over the chest.

Acceptable. Low angle with the lamp in the foreground, one Deccan fort stain with cannon behind his head, Ananthan look correct (topknot, temple grey, bare-headed, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain, conch knife, clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud). Minor issues: the brand on the raised left forearm is a crisp circular spiral or sunburst emblem, not a blurred patch of ridges. The temple grey is a bold white streak, but it matches 6.4. The caption fits on the plain red wall at top right above the doorway, or on the floor mat at bottom right.

Minor: the silver chain carries a round sun-face medallion that 6.1 and 6.4 do not show, and there is faint stubble texture on the chin. It still reads as clean-shaven, with the curled moustache, tiny gold stud, grey temples, crown topknot, conch-marked ivory knife at the left hip and the brand and scar on the inner left forearm all correct. He sits on the mat looking up-left toward the king, which matches the room in 6.1 and 6.4. The upper-left laterite wall is clear for both balloons.

Acceptable insert with continuity flaws. The mundu falls straight down in long vertical folds and the floor recedes well below, so he reads as standing, while 6.2 and 6.4 seat him cross-legged on the mat. The chain of office is a heavy rosette-link chain hanging to the waist, not the simple neck chain of the neighbouring panels. The thumb rests on the pommel just above the conch rather than over it. Through the doorway is an open veranda with trees, not the inner pillared corridor of 6.2. The hand is relaxed, not gripping, and its anatomy is sound (thumb plus four fingers, faint ridged nails). The ivory hilt shows the conch clearly, with no text or gore. Clear wall and dark doorway space on the right takes three balloons. Nagoji's head is off the top edge.

Acceptable and matches the script. Varma on the platform at left has the peacock-crest turban, pearl earrings and forehead mark, and sets the letter down beside him while studying Nagoji. Nagoji on the mat at right has the topknot with temple grey, mundu, chain, knife, clean chin and gold stud. Minor issues: at high zoom the inked mark on the knife's ivory hilt looks like small glyphs instead of a conch (a retouch to a conch would be ideal), and the brand and scar sit near the elbow, not just above the wrist. Varma's balloons fit over the wall and bamboo blind at top left, and on the plain red wall to the right of the bookshelf.

Minor: the face is only warm-lit, not dramatically lit from below as the script asks. Otherwise everything is correct: the cream-and-gold turban with jewelled peacock crest, pearl drop earrings, the white-and-red forehead mark matching his sheet, pearl and gold necklaces, gold armlets, bare chest and gold-bordered cream cloth. He leans forward on the red-bolstered platform toward the brass open-wick lamp in the foreground, eyes narrowed toward Nagoji's side of the room, consistent with 6.4. The dark pillared corridor at upper right gives clear space for both balloons.

Minor only. Varma's shadow is not clearly drawn as his own shadow across the mat: the lamp stands beside him rather than straight behind, and the dark band between the men is mostly the platform's floor shadow, though it does stop short of Nagoji. The camera sits at seated eye level rather than right down at the mat. Nagoji's long forearm scar runs up past the elbow onto the upper arm (it is on the correct LEFT arm and is not a cross). There is faint stubble shading on his chin. Varma matches his sheet: peacock-crest turban, gold armlets, pearl earrings and forehead mark. Nagoji has his greying topknot, moustache, gold ear stud, silver chain, shoulder cloth and conch knife. The room matches 7.2 (laterite wall, palm-leaf shelves, brass lamp, map, doorway to the corridor). The map shows no text. The plain wall between Varma's turban and the shelves, and the ceiling beams, give room for the balloon.

Minor only. Nagoji is on one knee with a hand on his knee, so he reads as about to rise rather than mid-rise. The two officers' heads nearly touch the top edge, so there is little corridor-ceiling space above them. Place Varma's two balloons on the plain laterite wall above his turban (about x 0.28-0.50, y 0.02-0.18) and on the upper map (about x 0.52-0.72, y 0.04-0.16), clear of Nagoji's face. Put the caption on the dark threshold step between the officers at the bottom (about x 0.28-0.78, y 0.86-1.0). The officers wear their knots on the crown, not at the front, and their curved blades are short. Everything else matches. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small gold stud, his topknot, the silver chain, the shoulder cloth, the ivory-handled knife and the brand on his inner left forearm. Varma is in the court turban with the peacock crest, the red forehead mark, pearl and gold necklaces and armlets, and gives a half-smile with a dismissive hand. There is one brass lamp, the map has no writing, and there is no painted text.

Minor only. The second foreground officer has grey temples and a moustache, which makes him look a little like Nagoji. Nagoji is still clearly marked by the silver chain, the shoulder cloth and Padmini beside him. Both officers carry staffs, which the script does not ask for, and wear crown knots. The sky band is narrow. Put the two short captions in the sky between the officers' heads and the palms (about x 0.21-0.45, y 0.0-0.10). Put Padmini's long speech in the sky and on the plain wall above her and Nagoji (about x 0.45-0.72, y 0.0-0.22), clear of their faces. Everything else matches. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a gold stud, his topknot greying at the temples, the silver chain, the shoulder cloth, the ivory-handled knife and the brand on his inner left forearm. Padmini has black coiled hair, a cream sari with a gold border and no blouse, gold jewellery and her stick, and she watches the carts. The setting is a daylit laterite fort yard with bullock carts being loaded and the gate open. There is no painted text.

Minor only. A faint vertical line on Nagoji's right upper arm could be read as a second scar; it is subtle. His chin carries light stubble shading. He matches the bible row: greying topknot, moustache, gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu with shoulder cloth, conch knife, and on the inner left forearm the puckered ridged brand with the white scar beside it (not a cross). Padmini matches her sheet: grey-threaded black hair gathered at the nape, gold necklace and earrings, a cream sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse, and her stick. Hands are sound. The carts roll out through the same gate and yard, which suits a redone 7.3. The sky at top centre and the plain laterite wall at left give room for both balloons in reading order: Nagoji high at top centre, Padmini lower left.

Minor only. The beat reads well: evening verandah, carved pillars, lamps lit, Revathi with arms folded facing Nagoji. Both match their sheets. Nagoji has his topknot, grey at the temples, gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, silver chain, white mundu with shoulder cloth, and the conch-marked knife. The brand on his LEFT forearm is drawn as a dark circular spiral near the elbow, not a pale puckered patch above the wrist. It has no letters and is not a cross. Revathi has a thin red streak in her hair parting where her sheet shows an ochre line. No painted text. The sky between the left pillars (upper left, above and right of Revathi's head) is clear room for both of her balloons.

Minor only. This is a tighter two-shot in the same verandah and light as 8.1: Nagoji's mouth is tight and Revathi's chin is raised. The scar and faint brand marks sit correctly on his LEFT forearm (the arm on screen right, with the shoulder cloth over his left shoulder). His chain carries a round engraved silver medallion that 8.1 does not show (it may be hidden under the cloth there). No visible sandalwood line at Revathi's hairline. Her arms are folded with her hands tucked in, which is fine. No painted text. Room for balloons is tight but workable: the roof and sky above and between the two heads, Nagoji's upper left of centre and Revathi's upper right.

Minor only. Revathi leans on a carved pillar, smiling with a playful look down at Nagoji's chest. She matches her sheet: sandalwood line, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets. Nagoji is now seated on the verandah floor, though he stood in 8.1 and 8.2; the script does not forbid it, and it justifies her looking down. His chain is drawn with heavier links and a round pendant, chunkier than in 8.1 and 8.2. The scar and brand are on his LEFT forearm (screen right). The knife is at his waist. His hands and Revathi's hands are sound. No painted text. The open evening sky at top centre and the roof at upper right hold both Revathi lines clear of both faces.

Minor only: the gold ear stud is a small round ball, a touch larger than 'tiny' but flush with nothing hanging; faint skin texture on the chin still reads clean-shaven. Matches the sheet and the ch19 Ananthan Pillai row (topknot with grey temples, no turban, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain). The beat works: a lingering half-smile with a creased, saddened brow. The setting matches 8.1 to 8.3: Velinadu verandah, carved dark pillars, brass oil lamps just lit, evening. No painted text. The medium caption fits in the upper right over the eaves and rafters (about x 0.6 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.18), clear of the face.

Minor only: he sits on the laterite steps at the verandah edge, leaning on a timber post, which still reads as the edge of the verandah of his quarters. The conch knife at his waist is hidden by his arms and the mundu folds. The ear stud is a slightly large round gold ball but flush. Topknot with grey temples, moustache, clean chin, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth all match. The wall niche with a brass oil lamp, the moonlit coconut palms and the glinting channels match the setting. Hands are clasped and feet sound. The large quiet moonlit sky at upper right (about x 0.55 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.35) holds both captions with nothing important beneath them.

Minor only: the build is heavier and more barrel-chested than the lean cavalryman on the sheet, and the chin carries a faint stubble shadow (it still reads as shaved). The head is cropped at the nose, which suits 'close on his hands'. Both hands have the right thumb side for palms up facing the viewer, with ridged discoloured nails. The ridged pale-pink brand and scar lines sit on his LEFT inner wrist and forearm (viewer's right), with no letters, and faint lines cross the palms. Verandah, niche lamp, palms and moonlit channels all match. The long caption fits in the sky at upper right (x 0.79 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.12) or on the plain wall at upper left, between the niche and the face.

Accepted with reservations. Seen over the shoulder from behind, the near (left) arm connects to his shoulder and carries the scar on the inner forearm, so the side is correct. But that hand's thumb sits on the inner side, so it reads as a mirrored hand. The far arm rises from the bottom edge over the mundu-covered lap rather than from his far shoulder. At reading size the panel still reads as Nagoji holding his hands out. The memory stain matches the beat: bandaged manacled palms gripping fraying rope, and Keshavrao's thin manacled hand gripping the hatch frame, with no blood. Topknot greying, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain. Caption space: dark blotched area at lower left (x 0 to 0.19, y 0.55 to 0.8), wet floor at mid-right (x 0.55 to 0.78, y 0.6 to 0.77), and the sky strip at top centre-right or the top-left corner of the storm.

Acceptable, with minor points. The script beat is met: three hands-only insets show the father's old thick-knuckled hands on a plough handle (with a dark kambal at the edge), the mother's turmeric-stained hands in green glass bangles rolling a stone roller on a grinding stone at dawn, and the brother's ink-stained fingers at a tied angarkha cuff drawing a single line with a reed pen by a brass open-wick lamp. There are no faces and no pseudo-text on the paper or book bundles. Minor: the plough beam in inset 1 does not visibly connect to the distant yoked oxen. Insets 2 and 3 start below a pale top band while inset 1 runs to the top edge, but that band and the dawn sky over insets 1 and 2 give clean space for the three captions.

Clean. It shows a thin moonlit surface line at the top, black water below, a wrecked hull, broken timbers, a split spar with loosely wrapped rope (not a noose) and loose planks settling on the sand. No bones, no body, no figure, no text. The large empty dark water from about 15 to 45 percent of the height holds both captions without covering anything.

Minor only: the grey at the temple is a fairly broad streak, and there is light tonal shading along the jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven with no beard. The brand on the inner left forearm cannot be seen because the raised left arm shows its outer side, which is fine at this framing. Everything else matches: thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, high Kerala topknot with no turban, plain white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain, and the ivory conch-handled knife at the waist. He is standing on the laterite-plinth verandah under tiled eaves, with his fingers at the wick of a brass lamp in the wall niche beside the door. The flame lights his face warmly and there is a low moon over palms and glinting channels. The art has no text. The open night sky at upper left gives plenty of space for both captions.

Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch19 row: curled moustache, clean chin, tiny flush gold stud, topknot with grey at the temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth, ivory conch knife; left forearm hidden. He kneels to set the pouch down, which reads fine. The sowcar's red pagdi is a little fuller than 'small' and he is bearded (matches 10.2). A small hilltop fort sits on the far skyline. The stall reads as a low cloth-covered platform rather than a counter. Note that 10.2 reverses the camera (Nagoji left here, right in 10.2). No text, no anachronism, hands sound. The sky at upper left and the plain awning cloth at upper right are clear for the caption and Nagoji's balloon.

Minor only. The beat is exact: the sowcar weighs the pouch on his palm with raised brows and points at the wax-sealed folded letter beside the scale. Nagoji sits across from him and matches the sheet: clean chin, curled moustache, small flush gold stud, topknot with grey at the temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth, ivory conch knife; left forearm hidden. He sits on a low jute-covered seat (not a chair). The camera is reversed relative to 10.1 (sowcar left, Nagoji right) and the platform reads a touch table-like. No text or legible marks on the letter, hands sound. The wide plain awning across the top is clear for all four balloons.

Minor only. It is a true over-the-shoulder shot: the right hand moves a reed pen across a sheet of wavy, unreadable ink lines on a low wooden board on a woven mat. The small brass inkpot sits beside it, and a brass lamp with an open wick burns high, warm and dim against laterite walls. Topknot with grey at the temples, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, small flush gold stud; the left forearm is out of view. The near-hidden jaw shows faint shading that could read as light stubble; at panel size it reads as shadow. The dark wall above the board and lamp (upper middle and right) is clear for the three letter captions.

Acceptable. A tight insert: the hand moves a reed pen along wavy ink lines (no letters or pseudo-text), and the page is about half filled. The brass spouted pedestal lamp with an open wick and the brass inkpot sit on the low board on a woven mat, against a laterite wall, in lower, redder light as scripted. The dark upper wall gives ample space for the one caption. Hand anatomy is sound. Minor: the ink-darkened pen tip reads slightly like a metal nib. Acceptable with minor notes. The over-the-shoulder framing onto Nagoji's face in low gold light is correct, and the gatehouse, laterite wall, niche lamps and sunset match 11.3 and 11.5. Minor only. The grey at the temple is a broad streak, a little more than 'first grey' but in line with the later-life sheet. Minor issues only. The framing is fairly wide for a half-width panel, so crop toward Padmini on the left to keep the smile readable. Her far earring reads as a small hoop. None. Padmini is seen from behind turning toward the gate, her hand on the stick. Minor only. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead sitting just at the lobe, a little rounder than a flush stud, but at print size it reads as a gold dot. Both are plausible for the same estate, but they don't match exactly. The beat is right: Nagoji, with topknot, white mundu, shoulder cloth and conch knife, follows Padmini through the gate. She has a black nape coil with light grey, a cream gold-bordered sari and her stick. The jackfruit tree stands ahead, and figures are lighting lamps along the verandah at dusk. The sky has little room left beside the roof, so the two captions should sit top left over the leaves and sky, or on the plain laterite wall at the right. The tiled roof band also works. Any of these keeps them clear of both heads.
